episodes.154652: A stalled front stretched from the northeastern Gulf into the Florida Big Bend into southern Georgia with a band of moderate to briefly heavy showers mainly over interior southeast Georgia. An upper level low over the northern Gulf invigorated convection lifting shortwave energy from the Gulf of Mexico along the frontal boundary which increased rainfall intensity. A Flash Flood Watch was in effect for portions of SE Georgia.
episodes.155297: Heavy rain of around 3 inches ahead of a cold front resulted in minor flooding in Tift county.
episodes.155516: Heavy rain brought flooding to the Ouachita, White, and Cache rivers.
episodes.155592: A strong westerly upper level jet over the northern Pacific was directed at the Washington and Oregon coast, driving a plume of deep moisture toward western Washington and northwest Oregon.
episodes.155593: A strong westerly upper level jet over the northern Pacific was directed at the Washington and Oregon coast, driving a plume of deep moisture toward western Washington and northwest Oregon.
episodes.164555: From December 29 - January 16, a strong and persistent Aleutian Low pressure system developed in the eastern Pacific which directed the jet stream and primary storm track at Washington State that resulted in a rapid series of atmospheric rivers and wind storms that battered Washington State. Water vapor transport into Washington State averaged 160-200% of normal during the period from December 29 through January 16. Numerous periods of heavy rain occurred during the episode, which in turn resulted in widespread and sustained river flooding, urban and small stream flooding, mudslides, and landslides in addition to the significant and widespread impacts from high winds, pounding surf, and coastal flooding.||During the wettest portion of this 19-day period, Washington State experienced widespread precipitation totals between 200% and 350% of normal. The prolonged bouts of moderate to heavy rain between December 29, 2020 and January 7, 2021, resulted in 8 major rivers exceeding flood stage; with 4 of them exceeding moderate flood.

events.narrative: Water was reported on several roadways, but no roads were closed.
Heavy rain caused minor street flooding in Pridgen.
The Bogachiel River was above flood stage Jan 3 to 4, 2021.

The Satsop River hit flood stage on the 2nd and Moderate flood stage on the 3rd. Flooding on the Chehalis River at Porter started on the 5th, cresting above Moderate flood before falling below flood on the 11th. Urban and small stream flooding occurred as well.
The Wilson River near Tillamook (TLMO3) reached flood stage at 0000PST, crested at 13.4 feet, then dropped below flood stage at 0930PST.  Flood stage is 12 feet.
The Chehalis River near Doty, Newaukum River near Centralia rose above flood stage Jan 3.  Urban and small stream flooding occurred as well.
The Willapa River at Willapa (WILW1) reached flood stage at 0345PST, crested at 21.2 feet then dropped below flood stage at 0800PST on January 3rd.  Flood stage is 21.0 feet.
The Skookumchuck River near Bucoda and Chehalis River near Grand Mound exceeded moderate flood stage. Urban and small stream flooding occurred as well.
Heavy rain caused flooding on the White River at Augusta for the first part of January..
Street flooding stranded vehicles along Circle Creek about 1 mile south of Seaside, OR.
